topic: Adani power unit resumes supply to Bangladesh
headline_marked: Adani Power Plant: [[Unit-2 resumes supply]] to Bangladesh grid
headline: Adani Power Plant: Unit-2 resumes supply to Bangladesh grid
summary: Supply from the Adani power plant in India has increased after a technical fault was repaired, though one unit of the Rampal power plant in Bangladesh has shut down.
details: The second unit of the Adani power plant in Jharkhand, India, resumed electricity supply to the Bangladesh national grid on Sunday at 12 PM.
The unit had been shut down since Wednesday night due to a technical fault in the boiler, which contributed to increased load shedding across the country.
Following repairs, the supply from Adani's two units combined exceeded 1,000 MW by 2 PM on Sunday, up from a morning peak of 760 MW.
The Adani plant has a total capacity of 1,600 MW, consisting of two 800 MW units. It has previously recorded supplies of over 1,500 MW based on demand.
Meanwhile, one unit of the coal-fired Rampal power plant in Bagerhat has shut down due to technical reasons, reducing its output to below 600 MW from over 1,100 MW.
Rampal officials stated that they are working to identify the cause of the shutdown and are attempting to restore production quickly, noting that there is sufficient coal stock available.
caption:
Adani's Unit-2 is back online! Power supply to the national grid is increasing, but a new technical glitch at Rampal plant hits production.

The second unit of the Adani power plant in Jharkhand, India, resumed electricity supply to the Bangladesh national grid on Sunday at 12 PM.

The unit had been shut down since Wednesday night due to a technical fault in the boiler, which contributed to increased load shedding across the country.

Following repairs, the supply from Adani's two units combined exceeded 1,000 MW by 2 PM on Sunday, up from a morning peak of 760 MW.

The Adani plant has a total capacity of 1,600 MW, consisting of two 800 MW units. It has previously recorded supplies of over 1,500 MW based on demand.

Meanwhile, one unit of the coal-fired Rampal power plant in Bagerhat has shut down due to technical reasons, reducing its output to below 600 MW from over 1,100 MW.

Rampal officials stated that they are working to identify the cause of the shutdown and are attempting to restore production quickly, noting that there is sufficient coal stock available.

Source: Dhaka Tribune, Prothom Alo
